changes.before:
When we talk about weather we do not only use simple present. We can also use will. Check the following examples.

TO CONSIDER 1. Will is used to state future. 2. Verbs go in simple form after using will. 3. A future time phrase may be added when the context does not already make the time clear. 4. Adverbs also help to state meaning.

Quick decision: “I'll take my umbrella.” Prior plan: “I'm going to take my umbrella because rain is forecast.”

Will – Future It will rain soon. It is cloudy. Will it rain soon? It is cold; it will probably snow later. Will it probably snow later? Go fresh, it will be sunny at the beach. Will it be sunny at the beach?
changes.after:

changes.after: Have you gotten it yet? One of the most difficult decisions in life is choosing who will accompany you for the rest of it. A lot of people dream of finding an ideal life partner; after many experiences, they may find one. Most of us would love to share our life with someone kind, honest and respectful. These are some of the good qualities we can mention. When situations become very difficult, they can bring out the worst in us, so it is natural that we expect to have a person who makes us come to our senses when necessary.
